note_claims.claim: Review of low mood, 4 weeks after starting sertraline.
Low mood for about 3 months.
Slight improvement in mornings only; mood 2–3/10.
Early morning waking at 4 am.
Reduced appetite with approximately half a stone weight loss.
Denies passive suicidal ideation (would be easier not to wake up) most days for the last two weeks.
No active suicidal thoughts, plans or preparations.
No previous self-harm or suicide attempts.
Protective factors include nephew and mother.
Alcohol use: Confirmed four cans most nights, more at weekends.
No drug use.
Mild nausea in the first week of sertraline, now resolved; no agitation.
Sertraline 50 mg once daily (4 weeks).
No known drug allergies.
Appears tired, reduced eye contact, and slowed speech.
Speech is coherent, with no sign of psychotic features.
PHQ-9 score is 19.
Moderately severe depression with partial response to sertraline.
Passive suicidal ideation without plan or intent; protective factors present.
Harmful alcohol use.
Increase sertraline to 200 mg once daily.
Referral to NHS Talking Therapies and self-referral details provided.
Inform the community mental health crisis team.
Review in 1 week.

transcript_facts.fact: Clinician greeted Daniel and asked who was with him.
Patient identified his sister as Laura.
Relative greeted the clinician.
Clinician asked if Laura could stay for the whole appointment.
Patient agreed to have his sister stay.
Clinician asked about progress since starting sertraline four weeks ago.
Patient reported feeling 'not great', maybe a tiny bit better in the mornings, but mostly the same.
Clinician asked how long he had been feeling low in total.
Patient stated he has been feeling low since the summer, about three months.
Clinician asked about mood on a scale of nought to ten.
Patient reported mood as three, maybe two on some days.
Clinician asked about sleep.
Patient reported sleeping badly, waking at four and lying there.
Clinician asked about appetite.
Patient reported not really eating and losing about half a stone.
Clinician asked if he was still off work.
Patient is a warehouse supervisor and is signed off for another two weeks.
Clinician asked about difficult thoughts, specifically thoughts that life isn't worth living.
Patient reported having these thoughts most days in the last couple of weeks, and thought it would be easier if he just didn't wake up.
Clinician asked about thoughts of ending life or harming himself.
Patient denied actually doing anything like that.
Clinician asked if he had made plans or done anything to prepare, like getting hold of tablets.
Patient denied having any plans or preparations.
Clinician asked what stops him from acting on these thoughts.
Patient stated his nephew and his mother stop him because he couldn't do that to them.
Relative stated that the nephew is really close to Alfie.
Clinician asked if he had ever harmed himself or tried to end his life in the past.
Patient denied ever having harmed himself or tried to end his life.
Clinician asked about alcohol consumption.
Patient initially stated he drank 'not much', maybe four pints a week.
Relative corrected the patient's statement, saying, 'Dan. It's four a night. I've seen the cans.'
Patient confirmed the relative's statement, saying, 'Yeah. All right. Most nights, four cans. Sometimes more at the weekend.'
Clinician noted that alcohol can pull mood down and make thoughts stronger.
Patient acknowledged the clinician's point.
Clinician asked about other drugs, cannabis or anything else.
Patient denied using any drugs.
Clinician asked about side effects from sertraline.
Patient reported mild nausea in the first week, which has now gone.
Clinician asked about feeling more agitated or restless since starting sertraline.
Patient reported no feeling more agitated or restless.
Clinician asked about the sertraline dosage and frequency.
Patient confirmed taking it every morning, 50 milligrams.
Clinician asked about other medicines and allergies.
Patient reported no other medicines and no allergies.
Clinician noted Daniel looks tired, has reduced eye contact, and slow speech, but is talking clearly and making sense, with no sign of hearing voices.
Clinician stated Daniel's PHQ-9 score today is 19.
Clinician interpreted the score as indicating the depression is still moderately severe after four weeks with only small improvement.
Clinician proposed increasing the sertraline dosage to 100 milligrams once a day.
Clinician offered a referral to talking therapies and self-referral details.
Clinician asked if he had to self-refer.
Clinician stated self-referral is the safest thing for now given the thoughts.
Clinician proposed reviewing him again in one week, not four.
Clinician outlined the crisis plan: call NHS 111 (mental health option) or Samaritans 116 123 if thoughts worsen or he considers acting on them; call 999 or go to A&E if unable to keep himself safe.
Relative agreed to put the crisis numbers in her phone.
Clinician asked if he would be willing to keep stockpiled medicines out of the house or have Laura look after them.
Patient agreed to hand stockpiled medicines to his sister.
Clinician offered details for the local alcohol support service and suggested aiming to reduce alcohol gradually.
